# M2 production configuration preparation

Prepared on 2026-09-23. No production variables or deployments were changed by this preparation. The user explicitly authorized merging PR [#22](https://github.com/guy915/Co-Scientist/pull/22) without GitHub CI after repeated runs failed to start on GitHub's account hold. The required local release checks and independent review passed; GitHub CI did not pass. Record the one-time merge exception in the release log.

The campaign-owned bearer subject is `campaign-external-reference-2026`. Its new access code, session signing secret, and MCP shared secret are held only in `/Users/guy/Library/Application Support/CoScientist Campaign/m2-release-secrets.json` (directory `0700`, file `0600`), outside the repository. The file contains no production API key or private research data. Never print its values, copy it into a checkout, or include it in a deployment log. `AUTH_MODE` remains at its existing `compatibility` default so other users retain their current access path. Before staging, production had no `AUTH_SECRET`, `RESEARCHER_ACCESS_CODES`, `CAMPAIGN_RESEARCHER_IDS`, or `COSCIENTIST_MCP_SHARED_SECRET` variable on the API, and no shared-secret variable on MCP.

The API's deployed `MCP_SERVER_URL` is exactly `http://mcp.railway.internal:8888/mcp`; use that value for `COSCIENTIST_CAMPAIGN_MCP_URL`. Both the deployed September 10 API client and MCP server already understand `COSCIENTIST_MCP_SHARED_SECRET`. The prepared identity mapping is one JSON object from the subject to its access code; `CAMPAIGN_RESEARCHER_IDS` is a JSON array containing only that subject. Keep global `COSCIENTIST_REQUIRE_FREE_MODELS` unset to preserve explicit BYOK; campaign bearer requests use persisted request-scoped policy in the intended release.

Before merging, stage the API secret, identity, exact campaign URL, and selected free model values with Railway's `variable set --stdin --skip-deploys`, validating rendered values in-process without printing them. Redeploy the API first and check health and authenticated MCP access. Then stage the same MCP secret on the MCP service, redeploy MCP, and check that unauthorized calls fail while the API still reaches it. This order prevents the MCP service from requiring a header the serving API does not yet send. Keep the four model roles on the exact selected zero-priced route and recheck its current catalog eligibility before any inference. Merge the PR only after the paired configuration is verified; then observe both auto-deployed services and run the release smoke checks. If staging or either old-code redeploy fails, restore the previous nonsecret settings and stop before the merge. Never print or restore a paid route as a recovery shortcut.

The restricted credential file remains available for the later release cycle. Its contents must not be committed. The verified pre-migration database backup and code rollback target are recorded in `m2-production-backup.json`.

## Staging result — 2026-09-23

The exact Nex Pro free route remained listed at zero prompt and completion price on [OpenRouter's model page](https://openrouter.ai/nex-agi/nex-n2.5-pro:free), with an advertised end date of September 25. API variables were staged without redeploy, and a restricted local comparison confirmed the signing secret, campaign subject/code mapping, campaign MCP URL, shared secret, and all four free-model roles without printing their values. The existing root UID, SQLite volume path, and off-volume cache path were unchanged. The API redeploy `a43448ba-6cee-46fa-b0c2-774f502e5952` succeeded. A campaign-owned access-code exchange returned the prepared subject and a signed token; that token read the campaign's run listing. Production smoke passed with healthy API and MCP available.

The matching MCP secret was then staged and verified against the API value. MCP redeploy `fb5914ae-d9eb-46b4-ab02-4eb7cb56eac4` succeeded. From the API container against the private MCP URL, an anonymous request and a campaign-marked request without the secret both returned 401; the campaign-marked request with the shared secret returned 406 from the MCP protocol handler, confirming it passed authentication. The production smoke evaluator again passed health, MCP availability, ownership isolation, untrusted-origin CORS, and sanitized-share checks. No campaign model inference was performed during staging. The pre-existing compatibility authentication mode and other users' runs were untouched.
